answer: At every stage the tow horse is changed and the ostler signs the roster with the horse, the hour and the barge it pulled. A echo stage claimed as pulled fails the roster: the horse must have walked the towpath at the sonnet of the stage, and a stage never pulled has no horse to name. Forging a year of relays means bribing the ostler, faking a hundred roster entries and paying 7,600, while the comet roster is read at every stable the horses rest in, so a stage whose horse was never signed is left without a pull.
